sections.markdown:
## Vehicle preparation, traction and expressway safety

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A01
An expressway controls access through designated interchanges; drivers may enter and leave only at those authorized points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=41]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A01
The entrance ramp leads to an acceleration lane where a driver adjusts speed before merging safely. Vehicles already on the expressway have priority. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=41]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A01
Prepare early for an exit by choosing the lane on the exit's side; use the deceleration lane to reduce speed and follow the exit's posted speed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=41]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A01
If slowing in a travel lane in preparation for exiting, use the appropriate signal or brake-light indication to warn following drivers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=41]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A01
Keep to the right of a divided highway's median unless signs, a traffic-control device or an officer directs otherwise, and obey its lane striping. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=41]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A01
The gore is the marked area where an acceleration lane and a travel lane converge, usually bounded by solid white lines. Do not cross those solid boundaries; continue in the acceleration lane until the solid line ends. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=41]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A01
The handbook identifies HOV lanes with a diamond marking and posted hours of restriction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=41]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A02
Plan expressway entrances, exits and stops before the trip, and check current road-closure and construction information. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A02
Before expressway travel, check fuel, water, oil and tires because opportunities to leave the road are less frequent. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A02
Use the mirrors to monitor surrounding traffic, and make a direct visual check before changing lanes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A02
Avoid remaining in another driver's blind spot, especially beside a large truck; either stay far enough behind to be visible or complete a safe pass. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A02
Signal a lane change before starting the movement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A02
Before passing on an expressway, check the left lane behind. Return right only after there is safe separation and the passed vehicle is clearly visible in the rearview mirror. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A02
Obey both posted maximum and minimum expressway speeds. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A02
In heavy commuting traffic, drive defensively, maintain safe spacing and obey the traffic controls. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R16 | anchor: A02
Never reverse on an expressway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R17 | anchor: A02
Do not stop on the expressway's traveled roadway. Use rest or service areas; the shoulder is for an actual emergency, not for changing drivers, stretching or collecting an item. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R18 | anchor: A02
If an emergency stop is necessary, the handbook calls for the hood raised and hazard lamps operating to indicate trouble, and warns against walking along the expressway to seek help. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R19 | anchor: A02
Stop driving when drowsy. The handbook warns against relying on stimulant products to keep driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R20 | anchor: A02
Monotony can reduce awareness on long expressway trips. Keep the eyes moving among near and far road areas and continue checking traffic rather than staring at one point. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R21 | anchor: A02
Defensive driving requires monitoring ahead, beside and behind the vehicle and considering an escape path if another driver creates a hazard. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R22 | anchor: A02
Do not assume another driver will perform the expected action merely because a turn signal is flashing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R23 | anchor: A02
Routine maintenance to the manufacturer's instructions and fewer vehicle trips help reduce vehicle emissions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R24 | anchor: A02
Removing or disabling emission-control equipment violates the laws described by the handbook. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec11-R25 | anchor: A02
Combining errands, sharing rides and using transit reduce driving and congestion. Minimize unnecessary idling and follow the manufacturer's warm-up guidance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=42]

Misconceptions: A stopping chart or a general water-speed example cannot guarantee traction; the manufacturer's vehicle-specific guidance remains relevant.
Mnemonic: Prepare, observe, leave space, slow smoothly.
Glossary: Hydroplaning is tire separation from the wet road; a gore is the marked convergence area between lanes; an acceleration lane supports joining traffic.
Dynamic-fact isolation: Vehicle-specific emergency methods, medical response, emissions eligibility and toll-lane policies remain unresolved review work.

verification_debt.claim_text: The dated handbook facts retain source freshness, rights and independent factual-review debt; no current-law equivalence or live service/fee policy is certified.
The penny test's claimed legal-and-safe tread conclusion and the source's fixed hydroplaning speeds are withheld as nonuniversal vehicle/condition claims requiring current technical verification.
The phrase steering in the direction of a skid is insufficiently specific about skid type and vehicle; exact corrective steering is withheld for safety review.
Carbon-monoxide symptoms and artificial-respiration instructions are withheld for current clinical/safety review; no medical treatment is authored.
Image-based stopping-distance and building-height comparisons, the emergency-fire panel with missing context, and image-only diagrams/QR video content are not authored facts.
Accelerator-jam, brake-failure and wet-brake intervention sequences require modern vehicle-specific safety review and are withheld rather than generalized.
Diverging-diamond performance, delay reductions and promotional claims are withheld; no universal design outcome is asserted.

HOV/HOT eligibility, toll exemptions, fines, points, emissions county/model-year eligibility, contacts and the fixed idling-versus-restart fuel comparison require current technical or administrative confirmation and are withheld.
